name: Question 18
worked_solution:
From the identity  $1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =2x+\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\ {tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})\text{d}x & =\int ({sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})-1)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})\text{d}x-\int 1\cdot \text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})-x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the identity 1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ with θ=2x+π6, we get

Substituting the above into our integral gives ∫tan2⁡(2x+π6)dx=∫(sec2⁡(2x+π6)−1)dx=∫sec2⁡(2x+π6)dx−∫1⋅dx=12tan⁡(2x+π6)−x+C.
